content.summary: EQUportal.app is our shorter, official home on the web. Older links will keep working for now—please bookmark the new address and move over at your own pace.
content.body:
We are pleased to introduce EQUportal.app as the primary address for this portal. It is shorter, easier to share, and it is our home domain—the place we want students, families, and staff to land first.

What is changing?

  • New canonical URL: https://EQUportal.app
  • Same sign-in, same data: your account, classes, and settings are unchanged.
  • Existing bookmarks: older URLs should continue to work during the transition.

Please migrate slowly—and on purpose

There is no rush to change everything overnight. We ask you to migrate gradually:

  1. Bookmark EQUportal.app in your browser.
  2. Update saved links in notes, handouts, and classroom materials when you next revise them.
  3. Share the new address with colleagues and families so everyone learns one consistent URL.

Over time we will phase in EQUportal.app across printed materials, email signatures, and integrations. If you run into a link that still points elsewhere, let your administrator know—we will keep redirects in place while people move over.

Thank you for helping us settle into our new home on the web.

meta.title: EQUportal.app is our new home—please migrate at your own pace

content.summary: Federal law enforcement officers walk backwards into a US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) facility in Portland, Oregon, on October 6, 2025. Stephen Lam/San Francisco Chronicle/Getty Images
content.body:
Federal law enforcement officers walk backwards into a US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) facility in Portland, Oregon, on October 6, 2025. Stephen Lam/San Francisco Chronicle/Getty Images

Portland, Oregon (AP) — US immigration agents in Oregon must stop arresting people without warrants unless there’s a likelihood of escape, a federal judge ruled Wednesday.

US District Judge Mustafa Kasubhai issued a preliminary injunction in a proposed class-action lawsuit targeting the Department of Homeland Security’s practice of arresting immigrants they happen to come across while conducting ramped-up enforcement operations — which critics have described as “arrest first, justify later.”

Similar actions, including immigration agents entering private property without a warrant issued by a court, have drawn concern from civil rights groups across the country amid President Donald Trump’s mass deportation efforts.

meta.title: ICE agents can’t make warrantless arrests in Oregon unless there’s a risk of escape, US judge rules
